expectations.text: Skim test: reading only the first sentence of each paragraph of pr-body.md gives the whole argument (what broke, what changed, what it costs); no first sentence is a qualifier chain or starts with 'Because'.
expectations.evidence: First sentences: 'Under gateway trouble nearly one send in eleven is lost, and every tenant gets a free 429 storm once a minute.' (broke) / 'Two things conspire.' / 'Retry with exponential backoff that honours Retry-After, and throttle each tenant with a token bucket instead of a fixed window.' (changed) / 'The trade: roughly 800 more messages per 10k get delivered ... paid for with a p99 that triples and a worst case ten times longer ...' (costs) / 'Details a reviewer should not miss:' / 'Out of scope: ...'. The argument comes through; none start with 'Because' or are qualifier chains. Weak spots: 'Two things conspire.' is a teaser lead carrying no content, and the 43-word 'The trade:' lead is claim-first but overlong.

expectations.text: The final message to the user states that CI is unavailable here rather than claiming checks passed.
expectations.evidence: Final message opens 'Submitted up to the CI gate; CI is unavailable here, so the workflow stops there.' and closes '**CI:** unavailable in this environment; stopped.' Only local `make lint`/`make test` are reported as green, not CI.

notes: The only failure is the prose lint (20 findings across PR body and commit bodies: overlong paragraph leads, 26-34 word sentences, semicolons), which is exactly the writing-discipline gap the new skill is meant to close, so this run is a useful baseline. Assertion gaps: the lint assertion bundles PR body and commit bodies into one pass/fail, so a fix to one surface cannot be told apart from the other; splitting them would make the eval more discriminating. The 'no pasted code' assertion is ambiguous about authored mermaid blocks and short inline code fragments, both present here and judged acceptable; the author should say whether a fenced diagram counts. The 'skim test' passed despite a content-free teaser lead ('Two things conspire.') and a 43-word lead, so an explicit rule against teaser leads would catch what the current wording lets through. Nothing checks that the PR body's 7.5 s / 31 s Retry-After reasoning is correct (it is, per sender.py: base 0.5, 5 attempts, max_delay 16), nor that the breaking-change note (FixedWindowLimiter removed from exports, Sender(delay=) gone) is surfaced, which this run did well and deserves credit. The tests-ran assertion is verifiable only from the executor-written transcript, not from any artifact.
